clue.text: See 7

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'See 7' with no group: the anagram in 7-down ('Rip-roaring EEC off') gives CARRIER PIGEON across both lights, but the file does not link 1-across to 7-down, so neither light can carry the whole wordplay.

clue.text: Delighted, having penny, to be hired out

parts.note: property hired out under contract has been leased

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at being rented out for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Being glad or happy about something is the same as being delighted by it.

clue.text: High tension gear upped in size

indicators.note: in a down clue, upped means the letters are read from the bottom up, so the run is turned round

parts.note: HT is the usual abbreviation for high tension, as on electrical warnings
a rig is a set of gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Electrical high-tension equipment has been made bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' turns the whole run HT + RIG, giving GIR then TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is a measurement round the middle, a person's or object's bulk.

clue.text: Cherry's neat pip?

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one
a pip is one of the suit symbols on a playing card, here a heart

explanation.surface: A cherry's tidy stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy, but it is the old word for cattle; 'pip' looks like a fruit stone, but it is a card symbol. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxheart is a variety of sweet cherry, named for its heart shape.

clue.text: As Yazidis for example out in the cold

indicators.note: out signals that these letters are put out of their usual order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: The Yazidi people, for instance, are left out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges INTHE plus C (cold) to make the answer; 'in the cold' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yazidis are a distinct people with their own culture and faith, so they are an example of an ethnic group.

clue.text: Slaughter tiger that's disembowelled smaller cat

indicators.note: with its insides removed, the word tiger keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: the ounce, or snow leopard, is a big cat smaller than a tiger

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene of a tiger gutted and a lesser cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaughter' is used in its sporting sense of beating someone heavily, not killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter an opponent in sport is to defeat them thoroughly, to thrash them.

clue.text: Put up popular nurse in secure shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is raised, written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: something popular is in, fashionable

indicators.note: in tells us the nurse goes inside the word for secure

parts.note: to secure a door is to shut it
SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A well-liked nurse is installed in a safe refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns the word for popular upwards, as this is a down clue; SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, is an old British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated corrugated-iron shelter, used widely in the World Wars.

clue.text: Rip-roaring EEC off to a flyer?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Rip-roaring EEC off to a flyer?' with no count and no group: 'off' rearranges RIPROARINGEEC to CARRIER PIGEON, spanning 7-down and 1-across, but the file does not link them, so no wordplay gives CARRIER alone.
annotationWithheld.clue: Rip-roaring EEC off to a flyer?

clue.text: Dissolute Proust in daze

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, signalling the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: The novelist Proust in a fog of debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolute' rearranges PROUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness, a dazed condition.

clue.text: Western world passengers on subway, miles out, take control

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it is placed after it

parts.note: the earth is our world

indicators.note: out means the letter for miles is dropped from the word for subway

parts.note: the metro is an underground railway or subway
passengers on a transport system are its users

explanation.surface: Western commuters riding the underground are told to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'passengers on subway' as one group of commuters; it splits, with 'on' placing the passengers after the shortened subway.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear the trousers is an idiom for being the dominant one in a household, being in charge.

clue.text: After time in dust mum's wheezing

indicators.note: after signals that the piece for mum comes after the earlier piece
in places the letter for time inside the word for dust

parts.note: ash is the dusty residue left by burning
Ma is a familiar name for mum; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: Mum is wheezing after spending time among the dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places mum after the dust-and-time piece; 'wheezing' stands for the condition that causes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory condition whose main sign is breathlessness and a whistling chest.

clue.text: Global computer stores and record company

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so the computer letters contain the rest

parts.note: PC is a personal computer
EMI is a well-known British record company

explanation.surface: A global business of computer shops and a record label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' looks like a noun for shops, but it is the verb: PC holds AND + EMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandemic disease is one spread worldwide, affecting the whole world.

clue.text: Love satisfied in river-it shows how far we go!

definitions.text: it shows how far we go!

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the river's name

parts.note: the Oder is a river of central Europe
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
to have satisfied a need is to have met it

explanation.surface: A romantic contentment on the river, with an exclamation about distance travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, from the zero score in tennis. The exclamation-mark definition describes the instrument rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's mileage counter records the distance driven.

clue.text: Frenchmen to restrain Welsh town villain denied female fruit

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the Frenchmen enclose the town

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation of Messieurs, French for gentlemen
Usk is a small town in Monmouthshire, Wales

indicators.note: denied means the letter for female is withheld from the word for villain

parts.note: a felon is a criminal or villain

explanation.surface: French gendarmes detain a criminal in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Usk is a town in Monmouthshire; MM (Messieurs) is the French plural of Mr, so it stands for Frenchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A muskmelon is a sweet melon such as the cantaloupe.

clue.text: Erstwhile partner keen to engage Queen's Counsel

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: to engage here is to take in, so the word for keen holds the queen's letter

parts.note: keen on something is hot on it
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A former partner eager to hire a Queen's Counsel barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's Counsel' looks like the senior barrister's title; it splits, with 'Counsel' the verb definition. 'to engage' puts R inside HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to advise or urge them, which is what exhorting does.

clue.text: Top milk producer

definitions.meaning: a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a knitted pullover
a breed of dairy cow from a Channel Island

explanation.surface: The best dairy farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best, but it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, and the Jersey is a dairy cow breed known for rich milk.

clue.text: Mining Derbyshire pit, he thought to offer Homeric description

indicators.note: mining means digging into the words, so the answer is found within them

explanation.surface: Someone in Derbyshire thinks of offering an epic description of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'DerbyshirE PIT HE Thought'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer used stock descriptive phrases such as 'rosy-fingered dawn', the classic examples of this device.

clue.text: Say a cart goes uphill — say how far?

indicators.note: in a down clue going uphill means reading from the bottom upwards, so the run is turned round

parts.note: eg, for example, means 'say'
a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A cart going up a hill prompts a question about distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes uphill' turns EG + A + DRAY into the answer; the second 'say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, the answer to a question of length.

clue.text: Dodgy satire in Lawrence's formal work

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside Lawrence's initials

parts.note: T E Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, was known by his initials

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A suspect satire appears in a formal work by Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: T E Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', is regularly clued by his initials; 'Dodgy' rearranges the satire before it goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: Eat cod

definitions.meaning: to eat is to consume or swallow food
to cod is to hoax or fool someone, a British slang verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' is a fish but here it is the British slang verb meaning to fool someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in food is to consume it, and to take someone in is to deceive them.

clue.text: City Diary ends with unforgettable poem

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
a log is a diary or daily record

indicators.note: ends means the first and last letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: A city diary closes with an unforgettable poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes the first and last letters of 'unforgettable', U and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, such as those of Virgil.

clue.text: Sudden cry rocks companion

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose rocks on a slope
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend lets out a cry as rocks fall.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a sharp, shrill cry.

clue.text: Chancellor's book about Islamic State force in revolution

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the book letters go round the rest

parts.note: BK is an abbreviation for book

indicators.note: in revolution means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to cram is to force or stuff something in

explanation.surface: A chancellor's book on Islamic State and a force in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' turns CRAM to MARC; 'about' puts BK round IS + MARC. The 's of 'Chancellor's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the first Chancellor of the German Empire.

clue.text: Regalia from electrified railway

parts.note: a live wire is electrified

explanation.surface: Ceremonial dress taken from an electric railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A livery is a distinctive uniform or insignia worn by servants or guild members.

clue.text: Shakespeare's sister in sex with Nordic man endlessly

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, written VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the Norse name is cut off

parts.note: Olaf is a common Scandinavian man's name, borne by Norwegian kings

explanation.surface: A tale of Shakespeare's sister and a liaison with a Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin for six, VI; 'endlessly' cuts OLAF to OLA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Twelfth Night, the shipwrecked Viola is twin sister of Sebastian.

clue.text: Tug

parts.note: the single word is printed in italics, so its letters slope like a structure tilting over, and a tug is a boat whose job is towing things

explanation.walkthrough: The clue relies on its typeface: the italic word leans, and a tug is a thing that tows. Apps that drop the italics lose half the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous tilting campanile of Pisa is described by slanted type plus a vessel that tows.

clue.text: Metal glowing that reflects dry stuff

parts.note: tin is a metallic element

indicators.note: something that reflects shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a glowing coal is red

explanation.surface: Shiny glowing metal that mirrors dry material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that reflects' turns RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinder is dry kindling used to catch a spark and start a fire.

clue.text: Daughters separately crossing junction get free

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: crossing means the word for separately goes across the junction, holding it inside

parts.note: each, as in 'a pound each', means separately
a T is a T-junction

explanation.surface: Daughters each crossing a road junction break away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts T inside EACH to give ETACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach something is to separate it, set it loose.
